title: Projective bundles of arbitrary quasi-coherent modules classify invertible quotients
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal E$ any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], without a finite-type or local-freeness hypothesis. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E)$ and $p:P\to S$, using the canonical symmetric graded algebra [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] and relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. The affine degree-one twisting modules [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] glue canonically to an invertible module $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. The degree-one maps give a canonical surjection $p^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_P(1)$, with pullback as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every scheme morphism $h:T\to S$, pullback of this quotient is a bijection between $S$-morphisms $a:T\to P$ and isomorphism classes of pairs $(\mathcal L,q)$ with $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module and $q:h^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$ a surjective sheaf homomorphism. Here $(\mathcal L,q)$ and $(\mathcal L',q')$ are isomorphic exactly when an isomorphism $v:\mathcal L\to\mathcal L'$ satisfies $v q=q'$. The bijection is natural under arbitrary pullback $T'\to T$; the morphism attached to $q$ has a quotient-compatible isomorphism $a^*\mathcal O_P(1)\cong\mathcal L$, and equals the canonical relative-Proj morphism of the induced graded map $h^*\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E\to\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map]. For any open $V\subseteq S$, $P\times_S V$ with its quotient and twist identifies canonically with $\mathbf P_V(\mathcal E|_V)$ with its quotient and twist. The map $p$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}$, $r\ge0$, this identifies $(P,\mathcal O_P(1))$ with $(\mathbf P^r_S,\mathcal O(1))$ [def-nagata-relative-projective-space, def-pc-projective-space-twist]; over $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ this is $(\operatorname{Proj}A[T_0,\ldots,T_r],\widetilde{A[T_0,\ldots,T_r](1)})$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-symmetric-proj-tautological-chart-gluing] to the given arbitrary quasi-coherent $\mathcal E$. Its degree-one charts give the glued invertible twist $Q=\mathcal O_P(1)$ and normalized surjection $q_P:p^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow Q$. Retain its frame normalization, restriction identifications and free-polynomial comparisons.

proof.text: For $h:T\to S$ and an invertible quotient $(L,q)$, [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map] constructs $F_h(L,q)$ from the induced graded map, on all of $T$, and identifies it with the canonical relative-Proj morphism. By [lem-trf-line-quotient-chart-inverse-pullback], pullback of $q_P$ recovers $(L,q)$ through $\theta_q$, and applying $F_h$ to the pulled quotient of any $S$-morphism $a$ recovers $a$. The same node gives invariance under quotient-compatible isomorphisms. Thus these operations descend to the stated isomorphism classes and are inverse bijections.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-line-quotient-trivialized-coefficients] on each affine W over V and every line trivialization. Its scalar and degree-one equations supply the existential ring map in the scheme quotient IsCanonicalMap predicate; its homogeneous coefficient equation and unit irrelevant-ideal image let the fraction-map canonical predicate identify the scheme map. Uniqueness already proved identifies each classified map with that fraction morphism.

For every $u:T^\prime\to T$, [lem-trf-line-quotient-chart-inverse-pullback] identifies the fraction morphism for the pulled quotient with $F_h(L,q)\circ u$, and its quotient isomorphism with $u^*\theta_q$. These equalities give the required naturality under arbitrary pullback.

Its free-module comparison identifies the pair with $(\mathbf P^r_S,\mathcal O(1))$ and over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the specified polynomial Proj and shifted-module twist. Finally [lem-trf-projective-bundle-separated] applies to this same $p$ with no finite-type or local-freeness hypothesis and gives separatedness.
